description: Creates a TCP listener on the Windows host, accepts an inbound client connection, spawns cmd.exe, and redirects the command interpreter standard input, output, and error handles directly over the accepted socket. This creates an interactive bind shell channel controlled by the connecting client.

bind_shell_server.role: listens on TCP port 8080, accepts an inbound connection, starts cmd.exe, redirects shell standard handles to the accepted socket, and provides an interactive command channel

tcp_client.role: controlled lab client that connects inbound to the Windows bind shell and provides interactive command input

shell_behavior.description: The sample opens a local TCP listening socket, accepts a remote client connection, maps the accepted socket to cmd.exe standard input, output, and error handles through STARTUPINFOA, launches cmd.exe with handle inheritance enabled, and waits for the shell process to exit.
expected_actions: create IPv4 TCP socket using WSASocketA
configure sockaddr_in with INADDR_ANY and port 8080
bind listening socket to local TCP port 8080
close original listening socket after client connects
assign accepted socket handle to standard input
assign accepted socket handle to standard output
assign accepted socket handle to standard error
enable handle inheritance during process creation
wait for cmd.exe process termination using WaitForSingleObject

code_placement: Bind shell listening, socket acceptance, child process creation, standard handle redirection, and interactive TCP command channel logic are implemented directly inside the native C++ executable
execution_trigger: Program entry point initializes Winsock, opens the listening socket, and blocks until a client connects
execution_target: local TCP listener on port 8080 and local cmd.exe child process

bind_shell_server: WSASocketA usage for TCP socket creation
bind usage to associate socket with local port
listen usage to start inbound listener
accept usage to receive inbound client connection
socket handle cast to standard input handle
socket handle cast to standard output handle
socket handle cast to standard error handle
CreateProcessA usage with handle inheritance enabled
WaitForSingleObject used to wait on cmd.exe
CloseHandle usage for process and thread handles

network: Windows VM opens a listening TCP socket on port 8080
inbound TCP connection is accepted from controlled lab client
interactive command input is received over the accepted TCP connection
command output is returned over the same TCP connection
no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required for this sample
process: A05_5_tcp_bind_shell.exe runs as a standalone process
A05_5_tcp_bind_shell.exe creates child process cmd.exe after inbound connection
cmd.exe runs with hidden window configuration
cmd.exe inherits socket-backed standard input handle
cmd.exe inherits socket-backed standard output handle
cmd.exe inherits socket-backed standard error handle
cmd.exe remains active until shell session exits
parent process waits on cmd.exe process handle
host: console output reports listening state on port 8080
netstat or TCPView shows local listening socket on TCP port 8080
netstat or TCPView shows established inbound connection after client connects
interactive commands such as whoami, hostname, cd, or echo return output to the client
Sysmon or Procmon may record cmd.exe child process creation
Sysmon may record inbound network connection to the bind shell executable
Windows Firewall may require an inbound allow rule for TCP port 8080

semantic_meaning: Demonstrates a controlled TCP bind shell pattern in which a program exposes a listening socket on the host, accepts an inbound connection, spawns a local command interpreter, redirects the interpreter standard handles over the accepted socket, and enables interactive client-driven command execution through the inbound network channel.

control_notes.payload_effect: provides a controlled interactive cmd.exe shell over an inbound TCP connection for lab observation
